name: Active Scanning - Wordlist Scanning
summary: Adversaries may use wordlist scanning to discover content and infrastructure through iterative probing.

name: Gather Victim Host Information

summary: Adversaries may gather hardware details about victim hosts, such as types, versions, and defensive components.

name: Gather Victim Host Information - Software
summary: Adversaries may gather software details about victim hosts, including installed applications and defensive tools.

name: Gather Victim Host Information - Firmware
summary: Adversaries may gather firmware details about victim hosts to infer configuration and patch levels.

name: Gather Victim Host Information - Client Configurations

name: Gather Victim Network Information: Network Topology

name: Gather Victim Network Information: Network Security Appliances

name: Gather Victim Org Information - Business Relationships

name: Gather Victim Org Information - Identify Roles

name: Phishing for Information - Spearphishing Link
summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages with malicious links to elicit sensitive information.

name: Phishing for Information - Spearphishing Voice

name: Search Closed Sources - Purchase Technical Data

summary: Adversaries may search DNS data for victim information, including name servers and records.

name: Search Open Technical Databases - WHOIS
summary: Adversaries may search WHOIS data for victim registration information.

name: Search Open Technical Databases - Digital Certificates
summary: Adversaries may search digital certificate data for victim organization details.

name: Search Open Technical Databases - CDNs
summary: Adversaries may search CDN data for information about victim infrastructure.

name: Search Open Technical Databases - Scan Databases

name: Search Open Websites/Domains - Search Engines
summary: Adversaries may use search engines to collect victim information through targeted queries.

summary: Adversaries may search public code repositories for victim code and information.

name: Acquire Access

name: Acquire Infrastructure - DNS Server
summary: Adversaries may set up their own DNS servers to support targeting and post-compromise activities like command and control.

name: Acquire Infrastructure - Virtual Private Server
summary: Adversaries may rent virtual private servers to make it difficult to physically tie back operations to them.

name: Acquire Infrastructure - Server

name: Acquire Infrastructure - Botnet
summary: Adversaries may buy, lease, or rent a botnet—a network of compromised systems—to perform coordinated tasks.

name: Acquire Infrastructure - Web Services
summary: Adversaries may register for popular web services to abuse during command and control, exfiltration, or phishing.

name: Acquire Infrastructure - Serverless
summary: Adversaries may purchase and configure serverless cloud infrastructure to make attribution more difficult.

name: Acquire Infrastructure - Malvertising
summary: Adversaries may purchase online advertisements to distribute malware or favorably position malicious artifacts.

name: Compromise Accounts

name: Compromise Accounts - Social Media Accounts
summary: Adversaries may compromise social media accounts to use during targeting, leveraging existing personas to engender trust.

name: Compromise Accounts - Email Accounts
summary: Adversaries may compromise email accounts to conduct phishing, spam campaigns, or acquire infrastructure.

name: Compromise Accounts - Cloud Accounts
summary: Adversaries may compromise cloud accounts to leverage storage, messaging, or infrastructure acquisition services.

name: Compromise Infrastructure
summary: Adversaries may compromise third-party infrastructure such as servers, domains, and network devices to use during targeting.

name: Compromise Infrastructure - Domains
summary: Adversaries may hijack domains and subdomains through registration hijacking or other means to use during targeting.

name: Compromise Infrastructure - DNS Server
summary: Adversaries may compromise third-party DNS servers to use for command and control or other post-compromise tasks.

name: Compromise Infrastructure - Virtual Private Server
summary: Adversaries may compromise third-party virtual private servers to use as infrastructure, making attribution difficult.

name: Compromise Infrastructure - Server

name: Compromise Infrastructure - Web Services
summary: Adversaries may compromise access to third-party web services to use for command and control, exfiltration, or phishing.

name: Compromise Infrastructure - Serverless
summary: Adversaries may compromise serverless cloud infrastructure to make attribution of operations more difficult.

name: Compromise Infrastructure - Network Devices
summary: Adversaries may compromise third-party network devices, such as SOHO routers, to support additional targeting.

name: Develop Capabilities - Code Signing Certificates

name: Develop Capabilities - Digital Certificates

name: Develop Capabilities - Exploits

summary: Adversaries may create and cultivate social media accounts to build personas for targeting operations.

name: Establish Accounts - Email Accounts
summary: Adversaries may create email accounts to conduct phishing or abuse free services to acquire infrastructure.

name: Establish Accounts - Cloud Accounts
summary: Adversaries may create cloud accounts to leverage storage services or acquire infrastructure without managing servers.

summary: Adversaries may create or tailor written materials, such as phishing lures or fabricated documents, to support malicious operations.

name: Generate Content - Audio-Visual Content
summary: Adversaries may create or manipulate audio, image, and video content, including synthetic media, to support targeting.

name: Obtain Capabilities

name: Obtain Capabilities - Malware
summary: Adversaries may buy, steal, or download malware, including payloads and backdoors, to support targeting operations.

name: Obtain Capabilities - Tool
summary: Adversaries may buy, steal, or download software tools, which may be open or closed source, for malicious purposes.

name: Obtain Capabilities - Code Signing Certificates
summary: Adversaries may buy or steal code signing certificates to lend authenticity to their malicious code.

name: Obtain Capabilities - Digital Certificates
summary: Adversaries may buy or steal SSL/TLS certificates to use during targeting and instill trust.

name: Obtain Capabilities - Exploits
summary: Adversaries may buy, steal, or download exploits rather than developing their own, to use during targeting.

name: Obtain Capabilities - Vulnerabilities
summary: Adversaries may acquire information about vulnerabilities from open or closed databases to use during targeting.

name: Obtain Capabilities - Artificial Intelligence
summary: Adversaries may obtain access to generative AI tools to aid in reconnaissance, scripting, social engineering, and payload development.

summary: Adversaries may upload malware to third-party or adversary-controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting.

name: Stage Capabilities - Upload Tool
summary: Adversaries may upload tools to infrastructure to make them accessible during targeting, enabling ingress tool transfer.

name: Stage Capabilities - Install Digital Certificate
summary: Adversaries may install SSL/TLS certificates on servers to enable secure communications during targeting.

summary: Adversaries may poison search engine optimization mechanisms to lure victims to staged capabilities.

name: Drive-by Compromise
summary: Adversaries compromise websites visited by targets to deliver exploits or malicious content through the user's browser.

summary: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in internet-facing applications such as web servers, Exchange, VPNs, and firewalls.

name: External Remote Services
summary: Adversaries leverage external-facing remote services like VPNs, Citrix, and RDP to initially access and persist within a network.

name: Hardware Additions
summary: Adversaries introduce rogue hardware devices such as network implants, USB devices, or wireless access points to gain access.

name: Phishing
summary: Adversaries send social engineering messages with malicious attachments or links to gain access.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
summary: An adversary sends a targeted email carrying a malicious attachment to gain initial access.

name: Phishing - Spearphishing Link
summary: Adversaries send spearphishing messages with malicious links to gain access.

name: Phishing - Spearphishing via Service
summary: Adversaries send spearphishing messages via third-party services to gain access.

name: Phishing - Spearphishing Voice
summary: Adversaries use voice communications to trick users into providing access.

summary: Adversaries move onto systems by copying malware to removable media like USB drives that are then inserted into air-gapped or disconnected networks.

summary: Adversaries manipulate software dependencies and development tools before receipt by the consumer.

name: Supply Chain Compromise - Compromise Software Supply Chain
summary: Adversaries manipulate software supply chain before receipt by the consumer.

name: Supply Chain Compromise - Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
summary: Adversaries manipulate hardware supply chain before receipt by the consumer.

name: Cloud Administration Command
summary: Adversaries may abuse cloud management services and APIs to execute commands on cloud-hosted virtual machines and other cloud resources.

summary: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, using its powerful command-line interface and scripting environment for malicious purposes.

summary: Adversaries may abuse AppleScript for execution on macOS, using its inter-application messaging capabilities to control applications and system components.

summary: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell (cmd) for execution, using the primary command prompt on Windows systems to run commands and payloads.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Unix Shell
summary: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution, using the primary command prompt on Linux, macOS, and ESXi systems.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Visual Basic
summary: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VB) for execution, leveraging its interoperability with Windows technologies and VBA capabilities for malicious tasks.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Python
summary: Adversaries may abuse Python commands and scripts for execution, using its built-in packages to interact with the system and perform malicious behaviors.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - JavaScript
summary: Adversaries may abuse various implementations of JavaScript for execution, using the platform-independent scripting language for malicious purposes.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Network Device CLI
summary: Adversaries may abuse scripting or built-in command line interpreters on network devices to execute malicious commands and manipulate device operations.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Cloud API
summary: Adversaries may abuse cloud APIs to execute malicious commands, gaining administrative access across cloud tenant services including compute, storage, and IAM.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - AutoHotKey & AutoIT
summary: Adversaries may execute commands and perform malicious tasks using AutoIT and AutoHotKey automation scripts to automate Windows tasks.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Lua
summary: Adversaries may abuse Lua commands and scripts for execution, using the cross-platform scripting language designed for embedded use in applications.

summary: Adversaries may abuse hypervisor command line interpreters to execute malicious commands, managing both the hypervisor and its guest virtual machines.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Container CLI/API
summary: Adversaries may abuse built-in CLI tools or API calls to execute malicious commands in containerized environments like Docker and Kubernetes.

name: Container Administration Command
summary: Adversaries may execute commands within containers using tools like kubectl exec or Docker CLI to run malicious payloads.

name: Deploy Container
summary: Adversaries may deploy malicious containers to execute code, bypass security controls, and establish persistence in container environments.

name: ESXi Administration Command
summary: Adversaries may use ESXi administrative commands and scripts to execute malicious operations on hypervisor hosts.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications like browsers, Office, and PDF readers to execute code on target systems.

name: Input Injection
summary: Adversaries may inject input events to interact with applications and execute commands as if from a legitimate user.

name: Scheduled Task/Job - Container Orchestration Job

name: User Execution - Malicious File
summary: Adversaries may rely on a user opening a malicious file to gain execution, using social engineering to deliver the file.

name: Account Manipulation - Device Registration
summary: Adversaries may register a device to an adversary-controlled account to establish persistence on a system.

name: Account Manipulation - Additional Container Cluster Roles
summary: Adversaries may add additional roles to a container cluster to maintain persistent access to victim accounts and instances within the environment.

name: BITS Jobs
summary: Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs to persistently execute code and perform various background tasks.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution - Authentication Package

summary: Adversaries may use network logon scripts automatically executed at logon initialization to establish persistence.

name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts - RC Scripts
summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by modifying RC scripts which are executed during a Unix-like system's startup.

name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts - Startup Items
summary: Adversaries may use startup items automatically executed at boot initialization to establish persistence.

name: Cloud Application Integration
summary: Adversaries may achieve persistence by leveraging OAuth application integrations in a software-as-a-service environment.

name: Compromise Host Software Binary
summary: Adversaries may modify host software binaries to establish persistent access to systems.

name: Create Account

summary: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access to victim systems.

name: Create Account - Domain Account
summary: Adversaries may create a domain account to maintain access to victim systems.

name: Create Account - Cloud Account
summary: Adversaries may create a cloud account to maintain access to victim systems.

summary: Adversaries may create or modify launch agents to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

summary: Adversaries may create or modify systemd services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by Python startup hooks.
